questions.question: Which ancient Indian dynasty built the city of Pataliputra?
questions.explanation: The Mauryan dynasty built the city of Pataliputra, which was the capital of their empire.

questions.question: Who was the founder of the Vijayanagara Empire?
questions.explanation: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded by Harihara and Bukka Raya, two brothers who were local chiefs.

questions.question: The Indian National Congress was founded in which year?
questions.explanation: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by A.O. Hume, a British civil servant.

questions.question: Who led the Salt March in 1930?
questions.explanation: The Salt March was led by Mahatma Gandhi, who marched from Ahmedabad to the sea to protest the British salt tax.

questions.question: The ancient Indian university of Nalanda was located in which modern-day state?
questions.explanation: The ancient Indian university of Nalanda was located in the modern-day state of Bihar.

questions.question: Who built the Taj Mahal?
questions.explanation: The Taj Mahal was built by Shah Jahan, a Mughal emperor, in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

questions.question: The British East India Company first established its factory in India at which location?
questions.explanation: The British East India Company first established its factory in India at Surat, a port city in the state of Gujarat.

questions.question: The Rowlatt Act was passed in which year?
questions.explanation: The Rowlatt Act was passed in 1919, which gave the British government in India the power to suppress any movement or activity that was deemed to be a threat to the empire.

questions.question: The ancient Indian text of the Arthashastra was written by?
questions.explanation: The ancient Indian text of the Arthashastra was written by Kautilya, a prominent figure in the Mauryan Empire.

questions.question: The Bahmani Kingdom was located in which modern-day state?
questions.explanation: The Bahmani Kingdom was located in the modern-day state of Karnataka, although it also covered parts of other surrounding states.

questions.question: What is the largest state in India by area?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan is the largest state in India by area, covering approximately 342,239 square kilometers.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers flows through the Grand Canyon of India, the Gandikota Gorge?
questions.explanation: The Pennar River flows through the Gandikota Gorge, also known as the Grand Canyon of India.

questions.question: What is the highest peak in the Eastern Ghats mountain range?
questions.explanation: Mahendragiri is the highest peak in the Eastern Ghats mountain range, with an elevation of approximately 1,501 meters.

questions.question: Which state has the longest coastline in India?
questions.explanation: Gujarat has the longest coastline in India, with a coastline of approximately 1,600 kilometers.

questions.question: What is the largest delta in India?
questions.explanation: The Ganga-Brahmaputra Delta is the largest delta in India and one of the largest in the world, covering an area of approximately 100,000 square kilometers.

questions.question: Which of the following is the smallest state in India by area?
questions.explanation: Goa is the smallest state in India by area, covering approximately 3,702 square kilometers.

questions.question: What is the name of the strait that separates the islands of Little Andaman and Great Nicobar?
questions.explanation: The Ten Degree Channel is the strait that separates the islands of Little Andaman and Great Nicobar in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands union territory of India.

questions.question: Which mountain range runs along the border between India and Myanmar?
questions.explanation: The Purvachal mountain range runs along the border between India and Myanmar.

questions.question: Which state is the largest producer of coal in India?
questions.explanation: Jharkhand is the largest producer of coal in India, accounting for over 25% of the country's total coal production.

questions.question: Which river flows through the city of Tirunelveli in the state of Tamil Nadu?
questions.explanation: The Tamiraparani River flows through the city of Tirunelveli in the state of Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: Which part of the Indian Constitution deals with the Fundamental Rights of citizens?
questions.explanation: Part III of the Indian Constitution deals with the Fundamental Rights of citizens, which are essential for the overall development of individuals and the country as a whole.

questions.question: What is the minimum age for a person to become a member of the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: According to Article 84 of the Indian Constitution, a person must be at least 25 years old to be eligible to become a member of the Lok Sabha.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of writ issued by the Supreme Court?
questions.explanation: Injunction is not a type of writ issued by the Supreme Court. The five types of writs issued by the Supreme Court are Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo Warranto.

questions.question: What is the term of office for a member of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: The term of office for a member of the Rajya Sabha is 6 years, with one-third of the members retiring every 2 years.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution deals with the Right to Freedom of Speech and Expression?
questions.explanation: Article 19 of the Indian Constitution deals with the Right to Freedom of Speech and Expression, which is a fundamental right essential for the development of individuals and the country.

questions.question: What is the name of the system of local self-government in rural areas, introduced by the 73rd Amendment to the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment to the Indian Constitution introduced the system of Panchayati Raj, which is a system of local self-government in rural areas.

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Indian Constitution features federalism, with a division of power between the central government and the state governments, as well as a parliamentary system of government.

questions.question: Who is the head of the Indian Judiciary?
questions.explanation: The Chief Justice of India is the head of the Indian Judiciary and is responsible for overseeing the administration of justice in the country.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Financial Emergency provision in the Indian Constitution?
options: To deal with a threat to national security
To deal with a financial crisis
To deal with a natural disaster
To deal with a political crisis
questions.explanation: The Financial Emergency provision in the Indian Constitution (Article 360) is intended to deal with a financial crisis, where the financial stability or credit of India is threatened.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental duty of citizens under the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: While paying taxes on time is a civic duty, it is not explicitly listed as a fundamental duty under Article 51A of the Indian Constitution, which outlines the fundamental duties of citizens.
